notes:
Lead summary: small SaaS company building an in-app chat assistant for SMB customers. Primary interest: fast self-serve Hosted API (public cloud).

Key pain: unpredictable 429s and unclear quota/burst behavior during marketing-driven traffic spikes — "newsletters" and morning support surges. Customer quote: "When a newsletter goes out we see short windows of 5-10x baseline traffic and users hit errors. We need transparent burst rules and a simple SDK backoff pattern."

Technical requirements / asks (copied from call):
- sustain short bursts up to ~200 concurrent chat sessions for 30-120s without failing user requests (expected normal steady-state ~10-20c).
- maintain median generation latency <200ms for system prompts (50 token outputs) under baseline; acceptable tail latency <800ms under bursts if graceful degradation available.
- clear per-key quotas & visible remaining quota headers; prefer token-based billing but want burst credits or automatic soft-queueing rather than hard 429s.
- want example client-side retry/backoff + jitter patterns for SDKs and guidance for exponential backoff vs. linear retry for streaming endpoints.
- want model selection guidance: cost-sensitive — prefer smaller/faster models for most queries, fallback to higher-quality model when quality metric degrades.

POC plan: grant 30k trial tokens, run 48h burst/load test, collect headers and 429 events, Redwood SE to propose batching/latency tuning, then iterate to pricing.

Internal notes: prioritize Hosted API docs snippets on rate-limit headers (X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset), recommended SDK call patterns (maxConcurrency=20, adaptive backoff example), and a short playbook for handling marketing spikes (pre-warming, short-term token bump requests).

Customer is price-sensitive; likely to commit to paid Hosted API if we can: 1) eliminate user-facing 429s during newsletter spikes or provide graceful queuing, and 2) show predictable monthly cost under expected traffic profile.
